references.text: Praises God who created the great lights—the sun to rule over the day and the moon and stars to rule over the night—a direct parallel to God's placement of the heavenly bodies in Gen 1:17.
Confirms that God established light and the sun, and set all the boundaries of the earth—corresponding with God's placement of the heavenly bodies in the sky.
The psalmist regards God's heavens, the moon, and the stars as placed by God—a direct link to God's act of setting the heavenly bodies in the sky.
Warns against worshipping the sun, moon, and stars which the Lord your God has allotted to all peoples under heaven—confirming that God placed these heavenly bodies.
Encourages lifting one's eyes to see who created the stars and leads them out—emphasizing God's sovereign power over the heavenly bodies.
Speaks of how the world was created by God's word, so that what is visible came from what is invisible—a principle underlying the creation of the heavenly bodies in Gen 1:17.
